Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-09-21 | AMZN | Underweight | -4.8% | -3.7% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Underweight: trim a full-weight position by roughly 40–45% at market near 258.45 down to ~55–60% of standard weight, and place the balance in scaled limits into 265.9–267.6 (target ~40–45%) with a 5–10 session fallback at market so the reduction never depends on a bounce. Ladder the residual on closing basis only: below 253.60 → ~45–50%; below 250.5–251.9 → ~30–35%; below 244.30 → ~20%; flat on a close below 240.4 (200-SMA). A decisive close above 267.6 on expanding volume with VWMA back above the 50-SMA and a MACD signal cross above zero invalidates the intermediate thesis — that is the stop, but size for gaps (AMZN gapped +12.5% on 7/31 and −8.9% on 2/6), not to the stop. No naked short and no new tactical long above the bull's 259.77 trigger; if the desk wants the range, cap it at 10–15% of standard weight near 253.6–256.1 with a 253.60 hard stop, labelled a trade. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored at the Q3 print over a ≥1-month window, but the 7.6% bandwidth squeeze should resolve within 1–3 weeks and takes precedence.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats converged on reducing AMZN, so the decision turned on magnitude and mechanics, and the neutral seat won that exchange against the aggressive's 50–60%-plus-tactical-long and the conservative's immediate cut to 25–30%. The bear/Research Manager case wins the points that price the equity and was never repaired by the bull: (1) the $650B "backlog" is a purchase-obligation ladder — supplier commitments for chips, content and compute — while deferred revenue, the actual customer commitment, is flat at ~$25.0B, and $78.1B of those obligations are due inside twelve months against Q2 FCF of −$8.8B; (2) capex of $54.2B versus adjusted EBITDA of $53.5B in Q2 (101%), capex at 27% of revenue versus 19.2% a year ago, H1 capex +72%, ~$120B adjusted OCF against $173B capex ≈ −$53B adjusted FCF, funded by $64.2B of six-month debt issuance, long-term debt +93% to $133B and Q2 interest expense +155%; (3) valuation was asked and never answered — ~32x trailing normalized EPS of $7.98 (reported $12.42 carries ~$4.44/share of non-cash private-equity revaluation), with the bull offering price levels instead of a multiple, forward EPS or return-on-capex; (4) earnings quality is correlated — the $122.3B non-marketable equity stake (from $16.2B) with $62.8B of H1 mark-to-model revaluation (~11% of assets) and a +$38.1B AOCI build against only −$1.56B of FX; (5) the tape is a failed repair, not a base — 258.45 sits inside the unfilled 254.83–259.77 gap with the 9/21 high of 259.49 rejected, MACD −1.54 below signal −1.30, 10-EMA 253.92 and VWMA 253.75 below a flattening 50-SMA at 256.10, lower highs 284.02 → 266.43 → 258.90 → 256.78, VWMA down from 271.91 on 8/19, and the bull's own setup is ~1:1 (6.17 points of risk to 253.60 against 6.13 to target one) with the genuine repair threshold at 266.4–267.6, roughly 3% higher. What keeps this at Underweight rather than Sell is unrefuted: Q2 revenue $200.6B (+19.6%, accelerating from +16.6%), operating income $27.5B (+43.2%), margin 13.69% (+226bp), gross margin 52.26% (+45bp) with D&A already +31%, a −64 day cash conversion cycle, $176.1B of cash and securities, price still 7.5% above a rising 200-SMA at 240.42 with the 50 above the 200, and a mark-based EPS air pocket being a multiple event rather than a solvency event — plus $122B of private stakes and Q3 earnings-gap risk making an outright short a poor risk shape. On execution the aggressive seat is right that the 200-SMA is not a shield but wrong that 265.9–267.6 is a reliable residual exit inside a squeeze and wrong to pair an Underweight with a 25%-of-weight tactical long, which the neutral correctly called a second position rather than a hedge; the conservative seat is right that stops get skipped but wrong on magnitude, since 43.2% operating-income growth, $176B liquidity and a rising 200-SMA are not distress, and the 9/21 first close above the 50-SMA and mid-band in eight sessions with RSI 39.4 → 52.7 makes a maximum immediate cut a sale into a two-way coil. Hence the neutral's staged, laddered, gap-sized reduction, with majority executed at market rather than queued above spot — the documented failure mode in this book. Upgrade toward standard weight requires all of: a decisive close above 267.6 on expanding volume with VWMA back above the 50-SMA and a MACD cross above zero; a capex plateau or decelerating capex with D&A growth below gross-profit growth for two consecutive quarters; growth in deferred revenue or a disclosed customer backlog rather than purchase obligations; and AWS segment revenue and operating income disclosed and re-accelerating. Move toward flat on a markdown or flat mark on the $122.3B book, total debt past ~$150B, a close below 244.30, or a close below 240.4. Explicitly not underwritten: AWS segment revenue and operating income (so neither the AWS >25% test nor capex ROI can be measured), capex guidance, forward consensus EPS, and quantification of the pregnancy-accommodation litigation, cargo-crash probe and warehouse wage announcement; with no portfolio, holdings or cash context, all sizing is a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN weight and must flex with the caller's aggregate AI-capex exposure elsewhere — trimming AMZN while holding NVDA/GOOGL/hyperscalers at full weight would be optics, not risk management.

**Price Target**: 246.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored at the Q3 print over a ≥1-month window; the 1-3 week bandwidth resolution (259.77 up / 253.60 down) takes precedence

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -3.7% (AMZN -4.8% vs SPY) confirms the Underweight directional call and took price to roughly the 246 target, but five sessions are far too short to validate the 3–6 month capex/FCF/earnings-quality thesis. This supports the bear tape read—failed repair inside the 254.83–259.77 gap, lower highs, MACD below signal—and the valuation caution, while leaving the capex, deferred-revenue and earnings-quality claims unjudged. Lesson: in a compressed-bandwidth failed repair, execute the majority at market immediately and treat above-spot ladders like 265.9–267.6 as residual-only, because the move can reach target before any bounce fills them.

[2026-09-18 | AMZN | Overweight | -1.6% | -2.9% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Overweight, but do not chase the 253.71 mid-range print. Build in stages: first add only on a daily close above 257.59 on at least 40M shares, sized about 5% of a standard allocation; a second add only after the Q3 print confirms capex plateau, stable margins and AWS/backlog evidence, keeping total exposure around 110-115% until then and reserving 125% for post-Q3 validation. On a flush, require stabilization and a reclaim of 246.39-249.20 before adding; a closing break below 239.82/200-SMA 240.30 invalidates the core thesis. Use a closing-basis 249.20 stop for the tactical overlay, trim one-third of the overlay at 261.12 and the remainder at 265.88, and re-score over 3-6 months at the late-October Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The bull wins the direction, but the bear and neutral win the execution, and that is why this is Overweight rather than Buy and not a mid-range starter.

The operating evidence is unrefuted and rules out Sell/Underweight. Q2 2026 revenue was $200.61B, +19.6% y/y and accelerating from +18.2% in H1; operating income $27.46B, +43.2%; operating margin 13.7%, +230bp; gross margin a record 52.3%. TTM operating cash flow was $161.40B, +33.3%, against capex of $173.03B, +60.7%, leaving TTM FCF of -$11.63B. That negative FCF is a deliberate AI/cloud/logistics build funded from $176.1B of cash and AFS securities and roughly $30B of net cash, not operating burn. The bear's earnings-quality point is real but largely neutralized: strip the $62.81B of H1 non-cash equity mark-ups and Q2 core EPS was about $2.16, +29%, still roughly 31x core and 26-27x EV/EBIT for a business compounding operating income at 43%. The $122.3B non-marketable equity book is a book-value risk, not a cash risk, and the normalized framework already excludes those marks. The primary trend is also intact: price at 253.71 sits +5.58% above a rising 200-SMA at 240.30, and the 50/200 spread has widened to 15.54, with no death-cross risk nearby.

The bear's genuine win is the tape and trade construction. AMZN has made lower highs from 287.20 to 255.43 and lower lows from 257.73 to 244.30, closed below the 50-SMA at 255.84 for five sessions and below the VWMA at 254.10 for twenty-five, with MACD still negative and no crossover and no RSI divergence at the 9/16 low. The 9/18 volume spike of 52.27M shares, 1.59x average, closed at 253.71 below the VWMA, the 50-SMA and the Bollinger basis at 256.13 — effort without result, exactly as the neutral and conservative analysts argued. The aggressive analyst's 2.3:1 blended reward/risk assumes the 249.20 stop survives, but that stop is only 4.51 points, or 0.75 ATR, against ATR of 6.04 and routine ±6-point daily ranges; it is inside the noise band. The conservative analyst is right that the fair comparison is equal dollar risk at a confirmation entry, not the same large size at a worse price. The neutral analyst's fix is the correct one: shrink the first tranche, use a closing-basis stop, and demand confirmation before adding. The pre-committed Tranche 3 at 244-240 is also incoherent as written — at 244 the bear trigger below 246.39 has already fired, and a stop under 239.82 would be less than 0.7 ATR away. A flush add must require stabilization and a reclaim of 246.39 or 249.20, not just proximity to support.

I therefore adopt the neutral/conservative execution over the aggressive/trader construction. There is no starter at 253.71: the first add waits for a daily close above 257.59 on at least 40M shares, which would reclaim the VWMA at 254.10, the 50-SMA at 255.84 and the Bollinger basis at 256.13 simultaneously. Size that first add at roughly 5% of a standard allocation, not the trader's 8%, and add a second roughly 5% only after Q3 confirms capex at or below Q2's $54.2B, operating margin at or above 13.7%, and AWS/backlog evidence. Keep total AMZN exposure around 110-115% of standard until then, with 125% reserved for post-Q3 validation. A flush into 244-240 is a separate trade requiring a closing reclaim of 246.39-249.20, with 239.82 as the invalidation line; a daily close below 239.82 on expanding volume cuts the tactical overlay back to standard weight and puts the core thesis in question. Profit discipline remains: trim one-third of the tactical overlay at 261.12 and the remainder at 265.88, leaving the strategic core overweight.

This also applies the prior AMZN lessons: repeated mid-range entries and support-test starters produced negative five-day alpha, and the 2026-09-09 reflection explicitly concluded that a lower-band tag should be a wait-for-confirmation event rather than a starter trigger. Waiting for the volume-confirmed close costs little in thesis terms and avoids paying up inside a distribution channel.

What would change the call: upgrade toward Buy on Q3 capex at or below $54.2B, operating margin at or above 13.7%, AWS re-acceleration or backlog disclosure, TTM FCF turning positive, and a volume-confirmed close above 261.12-265.88. Downgrade toward Hold/Underweight on a close below 246.39 on expanding volume, a close below 239.82, any markdown in the $122.3B non-marketable equity book, debt pushing past $133.0B while the current ratio deteriorates from 1.033x, or Q3 revenue growth materially below 19.6% with margin below 13.7%.

Data gaps are material and are not papered over: no portfolio, holdings or cash context was provided, so all sizing is relative to a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation; there is no AWS segment revenue/margin/backlog detail, no consensus estimates or forward guidance, no options positioning or short-interest data, no quantified Generac/Qualcomm warrant terms, and the news sample is incomplete. No external data or tools were used.

**Price Target**: 265.88

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -2.9% (raw -1.6%) is a mild negative for the direction call, but five days is far too short to judge a 3-6 month thesis built around the late-October Q3 print. What the window does support is the execution caution: refusing a mid-range starter at 253.71 and demanding a volume-confirmed close above 257.59 meant no entry into a tape that was still making lower highs, so the loss was in the rating, not in the trade. The lesson is to keep separating direction from entry, and to consider whether an Overweight with entry triggers above the market should be logged with an explicit "no position until trigger" note so the rating's paper alpha is not confused with a live P&L.
